chunker_findings.metric: v1 semantic chunker: share of non-whitespace section characters not covered by any chunk

chunker_findings.metric: v1 semantic chunker: papers with any uncovered text
chunker_findings.scope_note: First 20 corpus papers. The loss is consistent with the dropped-group merge bug (reproduced by a constructed property-test input); the individual snippets were not traced to it, so this is not proven per snippet.

chunker_findings.metric: Current semantic chunker: uncovered non-whitespace characters
chunker_findings.scope_note: First 20 corpus papers; real MiniLM; per-section chunking (677 chunks). Same papers and characters as the v1 rows above.

chunker_findings.metric: Chunks over the 256-token window when the cap is a plain regex word counter (measured with the real WordPiece tokenizer)
chunker_findings.value: layout 246 of 532; semantic 213 of 620; recursive 22 of 748; longest chunk 357 real tokens
chunker_findings.scope_note: First 20 corpus papers; current chunkers run with a regex-counting embedder stand-in (reproduces the old regex fallback). Not a claim about the v1 code itself.

chunker_findings.metric: Chunks over the 256-token window with the conservative estimator fallback
chunker_findings.value: 0 of 1,177 recursive, 0 of 931 layout, 0 of 976 semantic; longest 231 real tokens
chunker_findings.scope_note: First 20 corpus papers; ordinary scientific text only. The estimator is known to undercount accented/CJK stress text, which this sample does not contain.

chunker_findings.scope_note: All 200 corpus papers (first 20 papers only: longest 1,200; 35 of 764 chunks over 1,000). Bound depends on the two config values.

claims_log.metric: TEST frozen configuration D (recursive chunks, hybrid RRF k=60, weights 1.0/0.7, no reranker): nDCG@10
claims_log.scope_note: TEST split, evaluated once (`eval/test_ledger.jsonl`: 1 line). PAPER mode (Qasper's single-document task: the question's paper is given), 292 answerable questions from 124 papers; retrieval only, top_k=10; span-based relevance; MiniLM `all-MiniLM-L6-v2` at the pinned revision; local Chroma store `chroma_v2`. Not an answer-quality metric and not corpus-wide retrieval. Pre-registered primary metric (`eval/PREREGISTRATION.md`, sha256 `90dbf0e1…3531`).

claims_log.metric: TEST frozen configuration D: MRR
claims_log.scope_note: Same scope as the nDCG@10 row. Pre-registered secondary metric.

claims_log.metric: TEST frozen configuration D: HitRate@5
claims_log.scope_note: Same scope. Share of questions with a relevant chunk among the top 5 (a chunk is relevant if its character overlap with an evidence span is at least 0.5 × the shorter of the two). Pre-registered secondary metric.

claims_log.metric: TEST frozen configuration D: EvidenceRecall@10
claims_log.scope_note: Same scope. Mean share of a question's gold evidence spans covered by some top-10 chunk. Pre-registered secondary metric.

claims_log.metric: TEST frozen configuration D: EvidenceF1@5
claims_log.scope_note: Same scope. Paragraph-level F1 of the retrieved paragraphs against each annotator's evidence paragraphs, max over annotators (Qasper's definition applied to retrieval); questions whose annotators cited only tables or figures are left out. Pre-registered secondary metric.

claims_log.metric: TEST arm A (recursive, vector-only): nDCG@10
claims_log.scope_note: Same scope as the D rows (test, paper mode, 292 questions, 124 papers).

claims_log.metric: TEST arm F (semantic chunks, hybrid RRF k=60, 1.0/0.7): nDCG@10
claims_log.scope_note: Same scope. Different chunking strategy from D, so the comparison with D is a comparison of two systems, not of one factor.

claims_log.metric: TEST arm G (D + cross-encoder rerank of the top 20 fused candidates, `cross-encoder/ms-marco-MiniLM-L-6-v2` at revision `233902d2…bf0e0a`): nDCG@10
claims_log.scope_note: Same scope. G is not the frozen configuration; it is in the run only because the pre-registration requires "frozen vs frozen + reranker".

claims_log.metric: TEST comparison A vs D, nDCG@10 (pre-registered)
claims_log.value: −0.027 for A relative to D (A 0.430, D 0.456); paper-clustered 95% CI [−0.051, −0.002]; W/L/T (A better/worse/equal) 77/125/90; clustered p = 0.0320; **not significant after Holm** (m = 3)
claims_log.scope_note: Test, paper mode, 292 questions, 124 papers; 5,000 paper-clustered bootstrap resamples, seed 0; one Holm family of the 3 pre-registered comparisons. The unadjusted interval excludes 0 but the result does not survive the multiple-comparison correction, so it is not claimed as a difference.

claims_log.metric: TEST comparison F vs D, nDCG@10 (pre-registered)
claims_log.value: +0.006 for F relative to D (F 0.463, D 0.456); clustered 95% CI [−0.012, +0.024]; W/L/T 107/82/103; p = 0.5035; not significant
claims_log.scope_note: Same scope and Holm family. No detectable difference between D and F.

claims_log.metric: TEST comparison D vs G (frozen vs frozen + reranker), nDCG@10 (pre-registered)
claims_log.value: −0.058 for D relative to G (D 0.456, G 0.514); clustered 95% CI [−0.084, −0.031]; W/L/T (D better/worse/equal) 78/136/78; p = 0.0004; **significant after Holm** (m = 3): the reranker arm is higher
claims_log.scope_note: Same scope and Holm family. The dev split had shown no significant difference (D 0.500, G 0.481); the test result does not confirm that. Quality only: the reranker adds about 1.2 s per query on this CPU (next row).

claims_log.metric: TEST retrieval latency of D (retrieval only, not end-to-end): p50 / p95
claims_log.scope_note: `retrieval_latency_ms` inside `Retriever.retrieve` for 292 questions per arm after 5 warm-up requests, paper-mode filter, CPU only (4 logical CPUs, 16 GB RAM, Windows 11, no GPU), shared laptop under normal load, so the tail (p95, max) is noisy. Excludes any LLM call.

claims_log.metric: TEST retrieval latency of G (D + rerank): total p50 / p95; rerank stage p50 / p95
claims_log.value: total 1,242 ms / 1,942 ms; rerank stage 1,191 ms / 1,848 ms
claims_log.scope_note: Same scope as the D latency row; rerank of 20 candidates by the cross-encoder on CPU.

claims_log.metric: EXPLORATORY (dev, n=40, arm R only, no baseline, no noise floor): Answer-F1, short mode (max over annotator references), mean with 95% paper-clustered bootstrap CI
claims_log.scope_note: DEV split, one seeded sample (seed 0) of 40 answerable questions, Groq gpt-oss-120b at reasoning effort low, top-5 retrieved chunks (config D, paper mode). Abstentions count as F1 0. Not a published result: no oracle or title-only baseline, no repeat to estimate run-to-run noise.

claims_log.metric: EXPLORATORY (same run): abstention rate on answerable questions, short mode
claims_log.scope_note: Same scope as the Answer-F1 row. Four of the eight abstentions are yes/no questions.

claims_log.metric: EXPLORATORY (same run): citation validity in long mode, pooled valid cited labels over cited labels
claims_log.value: 50 of 50 valid; 1 of 34 non-abstained answers cited nothing
claims_log.scope_note: Same scope. A valid marker only means the cited source was provided to the model, not that it supports the claim (faithfulness would test that; the RAGAS scoring is incomplete: 2 of 34 answers scored before the judge's daily quota ended, so no RAGAS number is logged). The parser accepts the lenticular brackets the model used.
